title: Tiberias
hook: he is buried in Tiberias, visited by many

segments.voice: Yesterday, the physician's prayer. Your line: attributed, not his. A beloved prayer, and an honest label. Did you check whose words you were passing on? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

A lake in the north of the land of Israel, the Sea of Galilee, with a city on its western shore. Fishing boats, a promenade, hot springs, heat that hangs over the water in summer. And a short walk up from the shore, a tomb where people stop to pray, light candles and leave small stones. Maimonides died in Egypt. Yet this is where tradition says he rests. Today's word is that city.
screen: `A CITY ON THE SEA OF GALILEE.` → `CANDLES AND SMALL STONES.` → `WHY HERE?`

segments.voice: Tiberias. Turn it four ways. First, the journey. Maimonides died in Egypt, where he had worked as a doctor and led a community. Tradition says his body was carried from there to the land of Israel and buried in Tiberias. Legends grew up around that journey. Some readers see a wish behind it: to lie in the land whose laws fill so much of his code. Second, the stone over him. You met his epitaph early in this block: from Moses to Moses there arose none like Moses. Tradition links that saying to his grave. Tradition places other great teachers buried nearby too, so a walk through that part of the city passes through generations of learning. Third, what people do there. They come to pray, to recite psalms, to light a candle. Some leave a small stone on the grave before they go. The reasons people give for the stone vary: a sign that someone visited, a marker that lasts longer than flowers, a way of saying the memory still stands. Jewish teachers who speak about prayer at a grave often stress that the prayer is directed to God, sometimes asking for help in the merit of the righteous person buried there. Fourth, the blessing in a name. Proverbs says, "The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing." That verse stands behind the words said after the name of someone who has died: zichrono livrachah, may his memory be a blessing. And so his name, too, is said with a blessing after it, his name and a blessing in one breath.
screen: `FROM EGYPT TO THE LAND OF ISRAEL.` · `FROM MOSES TO MOSES.` · `PSALMS, CANDLES, A SMALL STONE.` · `MAY HIS MEMORY BE A BLESSING.` · then, large: `RESTING IN TIBERIAS.`

segments.voice: Breathe out slowly, and let the room go quiet. Bring to mind a teacher who has died. A grandparent, a rabbi, a coach, someone who taught you how to do one thing well. Picture the place where they rest, whether you've been there or not. In your mind, walk up to it. Set down a small stone. Say their name, and one thing they taught you. If you pray, you can add the words "the memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing." Then just sit with them a while. The bell holds the time.
Tiberias. A city on the Sea of Galilee, where tradition says Maimonides is buried, and where people come to his grave to pray. Today's word.
Your line: resting in tiberias. Today, say the name of a teacher who has died, out loud to someone, and tell them one thing that teacher gave you. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Jews visit the graves of family and of great teachers to pray and recite psalms, often leaving a small stone, and add 'may his memory be a blessing' when speaking of someone who has died.

notes: Burial in Tiberias after death in Egypt (Fustat) framed as 'tradition says'; legends of the journey mentioned but not told. Please confirm.

Epitaph 'from Moses to Moses there arose none like Moses' recalls day 1131; 'Visitors read it, or something like it, at the grave' kept loose because the current tomb's inscription may differ. Please check.
'Tradition places other great teachers buried nearby' (e.g. Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai, the Shelah) left unnamed; please confirm.
Custom of leaving a stone and the range of explanations given; phrasing kept soft ('Some leave a small stone'); please confirm.
Prayer at graves: the statement that teachers stress prayer is directed to God, sometimes in the merit of the righteous, is general; please confirm for this path.
Proverbs 10:7 JPS 1917: confirm 'The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing'.
Carry in the index is lowercase 'resting in tiberias'; kept exactly.

Editor: 'lived and died in Egypt' corrected to 'died in Egypt' (he also lived in Spain and North Africa); the motive for the burial is now 'some readers see', not 'what's clear'; the epitaph is linked to the grave by tradition rather than said to be read there; garbled closing sentence of the teach rewritten; practice opener varied.
